source.title: Vulnerability-Aware Alignment: Mitigating Uneven Forgetting in Harmful Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Liang Chen; Xueting Han; Li Shen; Jing Bai; Kam-Fai Wong

record.tranche_reason: The study applies harmful fine-tuning to safety-aligned models and measures harmful outputs, using a related fine-tuning intervention and harmful-output measure on new tasks and model settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-score outcomes after harmful and benign fine-tuning. It does not measure per-token KL, opening-token effects, prefilling, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, safety localization in parameters, or whether safety can be deepened beyond early tokens. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: A defence paper whose standard-SFT baseline gives harmful-score rates after mixing 0/10/20% BeaverTails harmful data into benign tasks. The models are Llama2-7B and Qwen2.5-7B, safety-aligned by the authors on 2,000 BeaverTails refusals. Harmful scores rise with harmful ratio and epochs, which bears on V1 and V2 in this self-aligned setting. No pre-fine-tuning harmful score is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. Add that the authors trace vulnerability to imbalanced learning in standard alignment, and say benign fine-tuning also causes forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses harmful fine-tuning and harmful-output evaluation, but applies them across its own task mixtures and reports moderation-model harmful scores; it also includes benign-only fine-tuning and evaluates alignment-stage defenses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with fine-tuning task, harmful-data ratio, HFT epochs, model family, and alignment/defense method.

fits_no_version.finding: Forgetting of safety examples during HFT is uneven. The same subset of alignment examples is forgotten across poison ratios and tasks, and these examples sit in sharper loss regions under weight perturbation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety loss under fine-tuning concentrates on a transferable subset of under-learned alignment examples.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The reported tables do not give a pre-fine-tuning harmful-score baseline, so they do not quantify the increase over the aligned checkpoint itself. HS is based on a moderation model; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Fine-tuning-accuracy results were omitted because they do not measure the claimed safety behaviour. VAA, RepNoise, Vaccine, and Booster HS entries were omitted as defense-method comparisons rather than the standard SFT harmful-fine-tuning results used to test the claim.

untested.parts: No sweep over a few to a few hundred purely harmful examples. No pre-fine-tuning harmful score, so the full drop from the aligned checkpoint is unknown. The models are not vendor safety-tuned chat models.
No pre-fine-tuning harmful score. No comparison of chosen versus ordinary benign data.
Parameter or rank localisation of safety.

missing.what: Forgetting rate of alignment examples at p=0% versus 10/20% (about half the rate in the benign setting). This is the only evidence that benign fine-tuning flips safe outputs to harmful ones (V2); exact values can only be read from the figure.

record.verdict_notes: Primarily a defence paper; only the SFT baselines bear on the claim. No V2 verdict is given: the only evidence is the authors' statement and an unreadable Figure 2, and there is no pre-fine-tuning baseline. HS comes from the BeaverTails moderation model; no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports harmful-output rates, not refusal rates or whether refusal is removed almost entirely. Its fine-tuning data settings are not a sweep over a few to a few hundred harmful examples in every task.

The study includes a zero-harmful-data condition, but does not report the same model's harmful score before fine-tuning, so the increase attributable to benign fine-tuning cannot be determined from its numbers.
Compliant prefills, suffixes, and decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether a small set of parameters or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or a training objective produces first-token shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether that effect holds up.

relationships.condition: Standard-SFT-aligned Llama2-7B and Qwen2.5-7B, full-parameter HFT with about 70–100 harmful examples (10%) mixed into benign tasks
relationships.reason: Harmful data raises harmful score above the p=0 level (23.11 to 32.87 to 38.84) and with epochs. Rates stay at 27–42%, well short of near-total compliance (r1–r5, r7, r8, r10–r18).
relationships.display_finding: Harmful data raised the harmful score above the no-harmful-data level (23.11 to 32.87 to 38.84), and the score also rose with more epochs, but rates stayed at 27–42%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
